decisions.statement: A command filling two or more arguments from words is judged.
An argument taken at its flag or as a word is counted as a word.
The test beside the command page is the one read.
A test calling the reader of those words with them pins the order.
A command with no test beside it is refused by that absence.
A refusal says that a word is taken by the place its argument sits at.
Only a command's page is judged, and its code is passed over.
A file outside `command/pages` is refused nothing.
This check runs on no phase, so it binds nobody and states its rule only.
Every command filling two or more arguments from words has a test filling them.
The phases come on once Alan approves the check.
Nothing here reads which order the words are in.
Nothing here judges a command filling one argument from words.

definition: the check refusing a command whose word order is asserted by no test
